title: Why is the main method public, static, and void?
shortTitle: Why is the main method public, static, and void?
keyPoints: public: the JVM must access it from outside the class – if it were private, the JVM could not call it
static: the JVM calls it without creating an object – no constructor runs before main
void: there is no caller to return a value to – the JVM uses System.exit(code) for exit status
String[] args: receives command-line arguments passed when running the program
The exact signature is: public static void main(String[] args) – any change and the JVM will not find it
Java 21+ allows unnamed main methods and instance main for simpler programs (JEP 463)

s1_definition.oneliner: public so the JVM can access it from outside, static so no object is needed, void because there is no caller to return to. String[] args receives command-line arguments.
s1_definition.profdef:
Each keyword in `public static void main(String[] args)` has a specific reason:

- **public** – the JVM invokes main from outside your class. If it were private or default, the JVM could not access it.
- **static** – the JVM calls main without creating an instance of the class. There is no object yet when the program starts.
- **void** – main does not return a value to any caller. The JVM uses `System.exit(int)` if the program needs to report an exit code.
- **String[] args** – the array of command-line arguments. `java MyApp arg1 arg2` passes `["arg1", "arg2"]` to main.
s1_definition.analogy: The main method is the front door of a bank branch. It must be public so anyone (the JVM) can walk in. It must be static because the branch operates before any customer account (object) is created. It returns void because the person walking in does not expect a return receipt – they start a process. The args are like documents the visitor brings through the door.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  java TransferApp SAV2001 CUR3001 50000
    │
    ▼
  JVM starts → loads TransferApp.class
    │
    ▼
  Looks for: public static void main(String[] args)
    │
    ├─ Found? → calls main(args=["SAV2001","CUR3001","50000"])
    │
    └─ Not found? → "Main method not found in class TransferApp"

  Why each keyword:
    public  → JVM calls from outside the class
    static  → no object exists yet at startup
    void    → no caller to return to (use System.exit for code)
    String[]→ command-line arguments
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
The main method signature `public static void main(String[] args)` is required because each keyword serves a specific purpose. Public lets the JVM access it from outside the class. Static lets it be called without creating an object, since no objects exist when the program starts. Void means it does not return a value to any caller – use System.exit() for exit codes. And String[] args receives the command-line arguments.

Change any part of this signature and the JVM will not find the entry point. The program compiles but fails at runtime with "Main method not found." This is a common trap for beginners.

One sentence to remember: main is public so the JVM can reach it, static because no object exists yet, void because there is no caller, and String[] args carries command-line input.
